thread:
eli_support: Hey — customer on Vercel Edge runtime seeing consistent 403 on OPTIONS (preflight) when calling our edge-ts SDK from the browser. Works in local dev + Vercel preview, only fails in production. They proxy requests from /api/proxy -> our hosted API. Network tab shows OPTIONS → 403.

sam_devex: Can you paste the fetch call and the preflight response headers? Is Authorization being sent from the browser? Any cookies/credentials?

eli_support: Snippet from the client (TS in Next + edge runtime):
```js
fetch('/api/proxy/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'authorization': `Bearer ${window.__REDWOOD_API_KEY}`
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt })
})
```
Proxy route (Edge function) does `fetch(REDWOOD_URL, { method, headers, body })` and pipes response.

maya_prod: Most likely the proxy is forwarding the OPTIONS to the upstream. Browsers send OPTIONS with no Authorization header; upstream may reject OPTIONS with 403. The correct pattern: handle OPTIONS in the proxy (respond with 204 + CORS headers) and only proxy actual POST/GET. Check network tab for missing `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization`.

eli_support: Net tab for the failing OPTIONS: status 403, response headers returned from upstream (trimmed):
```
server: Vercel
content-length: 0
x-upstream-error: missing-auth
```
No Access-Control-Allow-* headers. Vercel function logs show: `403 - missing api key header` coming from our edge gateway.

joel_reliability: That is consistent: the proxy forwarded OPTIONS upstream, upstream expected an Authorization header and returned 403. Two fixes: 1) Make the proxy respond to OPTIONS itself with proper CORS headers (Access-Control-Allow-Origin, -Methods, -Headers). 2) Ensure the proxy doesn't forward preflight to the upstream service.

sam_devex: Another nuance: if your edge proxy is doing a redirect or external proxying that results in an opaque response, the browser will drop certain headers. Also check Vercel's `headers` routes — they apply at edge CDN and can add CORS headers before your function runs. Adding those can mask the real issue (if upstream still refuses).

eli_support: Customer tried adding this to vercel.json routes but still saw intermittent 403s when traffic spikes; suspect SDK retry behavior/ordering causing two concurrent requests where one loses the header? They reported toggling to server-side-only (no browser involvement) fixes it immediately.

sam_devex: Which SDK version? We had a passporting retry change in 0.7.x that retries a POST and may run into preflight semantics in some proxy setups. Can you confirm SDK version and whether you're using the edge-optimized bundle?

eli_support: Using `@redwood/inference-edge@0.7.1`. Repro steps they've given: 1) Deploy to production on Vercel, 2) Open site, trigger generate, 3) watch network tab: OPTIONS → 403, then POST never reaches upstream.

sam_devex: Ask customer to reproduce with curl to see upstream behavior (bypass browser preflight):
```bash
curl -v -X OPTIONS 'https://<their-domain>/api/proxy/generate' \
  -H 'Origin: https://their-domain' \
  -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST' \
  -H 'Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization, content-type'
```
If that returns 204 with correct Access-Control-Allow-* headers, proxy is handling CORS. If it returns 403, upstream is rejecting.

joel_reliability: Also check that your edge function isn't forwarding `authorization` from the browser into the OPTIONS request to upstream. If it does, some gateways treat that as a naked auth attempt and reject preflight. The right flow: OPTIONS handled locally; for POST, add Authorization and proxy.

eli_support: I'm going to ask the customer to run the curl and share logs. As a short term workaround we recommended moving token exchange to server-rendered route (SSR) so browser doesn't call proxy directly. They asked if SDK downgrade would help.

sam_devex: Downgrade might hide effects but not fix root cause. We'll triage in eng-runtime: possible fixes: - make edge SDK attach auth only on actual method (not when forwarding preflight) - doc update for common Vercel proxy CORS patterns - add a debug flag to log when the SDK proxies an OPTIONS.

deploybot: Deployed canary → production 12% (today 04:22 UTC).

maya_prod: :thumbsup: ping @eng-runtime if you need access to the customer's logs.

eli_support: Thanks — will collect curl output and Vercel function logs, escalate to eng-runtime with the minimal repro and SDK version. For the ticket: customer id 9876, site https://example-customer.app, uses Vercel Edge with a single serverless route `/api/proxy/*`.

sam_devex: One more quick repro suggestion for support: in the edge proxy, short-circuit OPTIONS like:
```js
if (req.method === 'OPTIONS') {
  return new Response(null, {
    status: 204,
    headers: {
      'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': req.headers.get('origin') || '*',
      'Access-Control-Allow-Methods': 'POST, GET, OPTIONS',
      'Access-Control-Allow-Headers': 'authorization, content-type'
    }
  })
}
```
That will prove the issue is preflight forwarding.

eli_support: Great — will send that snippet and ask them to test. Will follow up once we have curl + logs.
